norms.heading: Record on Appeal – Uncertified or Disputed Record

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
(a) Uncertified Record. If the parties agree in a writing filed with the appellate court that either the legal file or the transcript is, or that both the legal file and the transcript are, true and accurate, certification shall not be required of that part of the record on appeal on which such agreement is reached, and that part of the record on appeal shall be filed by the clerk of the appellate court.
(b) Disputes about the Record. If there is any dispute concerning the completeness of the record on appeal, additional parts of the record on appeal may be filed pursuant to Rule 81.12. The filing of the legal file or the transcript shall not operate as a waiver by the filing party of the right to dispute the correctness thereof.
If there is any dispute concerning the correctness of any legal file or transcript, the party disputing the correctness thereof shall designate in writing to the appellate court those portions of the legal file or transcript that are disputed. Such designation shall be filed with the appellate court within 15 days after the legal file or the transcript, whichever is in dispute, is filed.
The appellate court, either on application or on its own motion, may enlarge the time within which any such designation shall be filed. The appellate court shall direct the trial court to settle the dispute and to certify the correct contents of such portion to the appellate court, and such certification by the trial court shall become a part of the record on appeal.

norms.heading: Exhibits

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
(a) If original exhibits are necessary to the determination of any point relied on, they shall be deposited in the appellate court by the appellant. If a party other than appellant has custody of exhibits, appellant may request that party to either deposit the exhibits with the appellate court or deliver them to appellant for deposit with the court. The party having custody shall either promptly deliver them to appellant or deposit them with the court. Respondent may deposit such additional exhibits as respondent considers necessary.
(b) A party depositing exhibits with the appellate court shall file a listing and description of the exhibits deposited.

(c) If it is impracticable to deposit any exhibit, it may be represented by photograph, mechanical drawing, or other means that fairly depict the exhibit.

(d) Original exhibits shall be deposited with the appellate court on or before the day the reply brief is due or when the court so directs, whichever is earlier. Any exhibits not timely deposited may be considered by the court as immaterial to the issues on appeal.
(e) Unless deposited exhibits are removed from the custody of the clerk within 30 days after the case is finally decided, upon prior notice to the parties, they may be destroyed or disposed of by the clerk. Exhibits shall not be destroyed or disposed of in post-conviction proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: Le conseiller peut imposer la mise en conformité des conclusions, demander des explications et assurer la communication, l’obtention et la production des pièces. Les Rules 84.04, 81.12 et 81.16 réglementent respectivement le contenu des mémoires d’appel, le dossier d’appel et le dépôt des pièces, mais ne confèrent pas exactement les mêmes pouvoirs au juge chargé de la mise en état.
correspondences.note_en: The French rule empowers the case-management judge to enforce brief compliance, request explanations, and control the communication, obtaining, and production of evidence. Rules 84.04, 81.12, and 81.16 address appellate briefs, the appellate record, and exhibits, but do not grant the same comprehensive case-management powers.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la notification simultanée des conclusions et pièces, le dépôt d’une copie au greffe avec preuve de notification et l’irrecevabilité des pièces soutenant des conclusions irrecevables. Les règles du Missouri organisent la notification, le dépôt et le dépôt des pièces, sans prévoir cette simultanéité ni cette sanction spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires simultaneous service of briefs and exhibits, filing a copy with proof of service, and inadmissibility of exhibits supporting inadmissible briefs. Missouri rules address service, filing, and appellate exhibits, but not the same simultaneity or sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 81.16 organise le dépôt des pièces originales nécessaires à la décision en appel, notamment à la date fixée par la règle ou par la cour. Elle ne prévoit toutefois pas une demande ciblée du conseiller rapporteur à l’avocat du demandeur.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 81.16 governs depositing original exhibits necessary to appellate decision, by the rule’s deadline or as directed by the court. It does not provide for the reporting judge’s targeted request to the petitioner’s lawyer.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose de joindre les pièces justificatives et les dernières écritures déposées devant les juridictions concernées, avec des justificatifs particuliers du lien familial ou successoral. Les Rules 81.12 et 81.16 organisent la constitution du dossier d’appel et le dépôt des pièces, mais ne prévoient pas ces exigences documentaires précises.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires supporting documents and copies of the parties’ latest pleadings before the relevant courts, with specific proof of family or succession status. Rules 81.12 and 81.16 govern the appellate record and exhibits, but do not impose these precise documentary requirements.

norms.heading: Record on Appeal – Reviewing Legal Effect of Instructions, Evidence Not Necessary, When

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
When an appellant desires only to have reviewed legal questions with respect to instructions given or refused and a review of the evidence is unnecessary to pass on those legal questions it is not necessary for the appellant to include the evidence in the record on appeal. In such case the appellant shall serve upon the respondent and file in the appellate court, within thirty days after the filing of the last notice of appeal, a designation of the parts of the trial record, proceedings, and evidence which the appellant intends to include in the record on appeal and a statement of the issues the appellant intends to present on appeal.
The statement shall show what material fact or facts the evidence tended to prove. If the respondent considers other parts of the trial record, proceedings, and evidence to be necessary, the respondent shall, within ten days after the service of the statement of appellant, serve upon the appellant and file in the appellate court a designation of additional parts which the respondent intends to include in the record on appeal and any additional issues the respondent intends to present on appeal.
Failure of the respondent to serve and file such indication shall constitute an admission and agreement that the respondent agrees that the statement is correct and that a transcript of the evidence need not be included in the record on appeal.

norms.heading: Time for Filing of Record on Appeal

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
The record on appeal shall be filed with the appellate court:

(a) If the record on appeal consists only of a legal file, within thirty days from the date of the filing of the notice of appeal in the trial court;

(b) In all other cases, within ninety days from the date of the filing of the notice of appeal in the trial court.
If more than one appeal is taken from the same judgment to the same appellate court, the time for filing shall date from the filing of the last notice of appeal in the trial court.

Rules 81.12 and 512.110 govern the contents and transmission of an appellate record, but primarily place preparation duties on the appellant and do not reproduce the same clerk-transmission obligation.

La Rule 44.01(b), RSMo 512.140 et la Rule 81.20 permettent certaines extensions, mais dans des domaines et sous des conditions différentes, sans règle générale équivalente.
correspondences.note_en: Article 645 makes the extensions under Articles 643 and 644 generally applicable, subject to express exceptions, especially for election appeals. Rule 44.01(b), RSMo 512.140, and Rule 81.20 authorize extensions in specified contexts, but do not provide the same general rule or election-specific limitation.

norms.heading: Parties Ineligible to File Documents Through the Electronic Filing System

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
(a) Applicable Rules for Ineligible Parties. Those who are ineligible to file documents through the electronic filing system shall comply with all provisions of Rules 81 to 84 except, to the extent the requirements in this Rule 81.21 replace them for formatting and filing the documents.

(b) Format and Filing of Paper Documents – Generally. Documents filed on paper shall conform to the following provisions:
(1) Documents shall be printed on one side of paper, size 8 1/2 X 11 inches, weighing between 18 and 24 pounds to the ream;

(2) Documents shall be secured by affixing a temporary binding such as a rubber band or a binder clip but not with adhesive tape, staples, spiral binding, or edge sealing products; and
(3) Except as provided by local court rule, only the original document shall be filed in the clerk's office.

(c) Legal File Volume Page Limit. A paper legal file volume shall not exceed 200 pages.

(d) Filing of Paper Transcript. A party who files a paper transcript shall also file the electronic medium provided by the court reporter. The reporter or transcriber shall certify that the electronic copy has been scanned for viruses and that it is virus-free. The appellate court, on motion, may make such order respecting delivery of paper copies of the transcript as may be just and equitable.
(e) Typewritten Documents. Any person unable to produce documents as provided by Rule 84.03 may file typewritten documents.

(1) A typewritten document shall:

(A) Use fixed space type not less than a ten pitch and ten characters to the inch; and

(B) Be double-spaced, except that the cover, certificate of service, and signature block may be single-spaced.
(2) If the typewritten document is a brief, it shall not exceed the following page limitations:

(A) Appellant's brief and all briefs in a cross appeal except the reply brief, 100 pages;

(B) Respondent's brief, 90 pages; and

(C) Reply brief, 25 pages.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la remise électronique des actes devant la cour d’appel, prévoit une exception en cas d’impossibilité étrangère et organise le dépôt papier, la date de dépôt et les avis électroniques. Les règles du Missouri imposent largement le dépôt électronique et prévoient le dépôt papier et la notification électronique, mais sans reprendre toutes ces modalités ni la sanction française.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires electronic filing in the court of appeal, provides a paper-filing exception for an external impediment, and regulates filing dates and electronic notices. Missouri rules broadly require electronic filing and provide for paper filing and electronic notice, but do not reproduce all these procedures or the French sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exclut le défenseur syndical de l’obligation électronique et organise pour lui le dépôt papier, les exemplaires et le récépissé postal. Les règles du Missouri traitent les parties inéligibles au dépôt électronique et leurs modalités de dépôt et de notification, sans viser une catégorie identique ni reprendre les règles particulières d’exemplaires et de récépissé.
correspondences.note_en: The article exempts the union representative from electronic filing and regulates paper filing, copies, and postal receipts. Missouri rules address parties ineligible for electronic filing and their filing and service procedures, but do not identify the same category or reproduce the specific copy and receipt requirements.

norms.heading: Appeals, When and How Taken – Expedited

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 81 — Appeals

norms.text:
Time Shortened by Court or Motion. Any time after the notice of appeal is filed with the clerk of the trial court, the trial court, on its own motion, or on the motion of any party, for good cause shown, may shorten the 30-day period provided for in Rule 75.01. The motion shall be supported by an affidavit stating reasons why the party would be prejudiced by the 30-day period before the judgment would be final for purposes of appeal under Rule 75.01.

If the trial court overrules the motion, the party seeking to shorten the 30-day period may file a similar motion in the appropriate appellate court, which shall decide the matter without deference to the trial court's denial. The provisions of this rule do not apply to judgments resolving fewer than all the remaining claims or parties as provided for in Rule 74.01(b).

correspondences.note_fr: Le président peut, en urgence, réduire certains délais, fixer l’audience sur la QPC et aviser le procureur général. La Rule 81.045 permet au tribunal de réduire, pour bonne cause, le délai d’appel, mais ne prévoit ni la fixation d’une audience sur une QPC ni l’avis au procureur général.
correspondences.note_en: In an urgent case, the presiding judge may shorten specified time limits, set the hearing date on the constitutional question, and notify the public prosecutor. Rule 81.045 permits the court to shorten the appeal period for good cause, but does not address a constitutional-question hearing or notice to the prosecutor.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose un jugement rapide, rendu en premier et dernier ressort, avec un pourvoi en cassation dans les quinze jours de la notification. Les Rules 81.04 et 81.05 et le RSMo 512.050 organisent les délais d’appel et la finalité du jugement selon des délais et effets différents; la Rule 81.045 permet seulement de raccourcir le délai de finalité dans certains cas.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a prompt judgment, rendered at a single level of jurisdiction, with a fifteen-day cassation period from notification. Rules 81.04 and 81.05 and RSMo 512.050 govern appeal deadlines and finality under materially different periods and effects; Rule 81.045 only permits shortening finality time in specified circumstances.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 918 fixe le contenu de la requête à jour fixe. La Rule 81.045 exige plutôt une motion appuyée d’un affidavit exposant le préjudice lié au délai de 30 jours ; elle ne reprend pas les exigences françaises relatives aux conclusions, pièces et copie de la décision.
correspondences.note_en: Article 918 specifies the contents of a petition for a fixed-date appeal. Rule 81.045 instead requires a motion supported by an affidavit explaining prejudice from the 30-day period; it does not reproduce the French requirements concerning merits claims, exhibits, or the decision.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise une procédure urgente pour les contestations relatives aux funérailles : saisine du tribunal, décision sous vingt-quatre heures, appel immédiat et sans avocat, puis notification au maire. Les textes du Missouri couvrent séparément l’introduction de l’action, la forme et la notification de l’appel, ainsi que la possibilité d’abréger certains délais, mais ne prévoient pas ce régime funéraire spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes an expedited procedure for funeral disputes: commencement before the trial court, a decision within 24 hours, an immediate appeal without counsel, and notification to the mayor. The Missouri provisions separately address commencement, appeal filing and notice, and shortening certain deadlines, but do not create this specific funeral-dispute procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise une procédure accélérée au fond, impose l’observation préalable des parties en cas de mesure relevée d’office et fixe les voies et délais de recours. La Rule 55.30 traite de l’audiencement et de la décision rapide des motions, tandis que la Rule 81.045 permet d’abréger certains délais d’appel, sans reproduire l’ensemble du régime.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes an expedited merits procedure, requires prior submissions from the parties before certain measures are taken on the court’s own initiative, and sets appeal and cassation routes and deadlines. Rule 55.30 addresses prompt motion hearings, while Rule 81.045 permits shortening certain appeal-related periods, but neither reproduces the full regime.

norms.heading: State Courts Administrator

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rule 82

norms.text:
(a) Duties. Under the authority and supervision of this Court, the state courts administrator shall have the following duties:

(1) Promulgate and administer the administrative methods and systems adopted by this Court for use in the office of the clerks of the various state and municipal courts.

(2) Make recommendations from time to time concerning the administrative methods and systems used in the office of the clerks of the various state and municipal courts.
(3) Assemble information concerning the current state of dockets, determine where assistance is needed and recommend assignment of judges.

(4) Collect and publish reports of business transacted by the courts, the state of dockets and court facilities.

(5) Prepare and submit budget estimates of the state appropriations necessary for the maintenance and operation of the judicial system.
(6) Administer the payment of state monies appropriated for the maintenance and operation of the judicial system.

(7) Develop and administer programs of judicial education.

(8) Process requests for transfer of judges.

(9) Perform duties required under administrative rule of the Court.

(b) Prohibition Against Practice of Law. The state courts administrator and employees of the office shall not engage in the practice of law or do any law business.
(c) Prohibition Against Political Activity. The state courts administrator and employees of the office shall not directly or indirectly make any contributions to or hold any office in a political party or organization or take part in any political campaign, nor shall any employee be hired or discharged on a political or party basis.
(d) Oath. Before assuming the duties of the office, the state courts administrator shall take and subscribe to an oath to support the Constitution of the United States and the State of Missouri, and faithfully to demean himself or herself while in the office, and that the person will not disclose or reveal any fact or information obtained relating to any case, matter, opinion or proceeding pending in court before the same has been made public by this Court.

norms.heading: Transfer Upon Application Prior to Disposition by Court of Appeals

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 83 — Transfers From Court of Appeals to this Court

norms.text:
This Court on its own motion or on application of a party may transfer to this Court from the court of appeals a case in which there has been no disposition. The transfer shall be for any of the reasons stated in Rule 83.02 or for the purpose of equalizing the workload of the appellate courts.

Any party requesting such transfer shall file an application in this Court within ten days after the filing of the record on appeal in the court of appeals. In connection with the consideration of an application for transfer under this Rule 83.01, this Court may order the record on appeal forwarded to it.
Applications for transfer filed pursuant to this Rule 83.01 shall not affect the time for filing briefs unless this Court so orders. In the event of transfer under this Rule 83.01, briefs already filed in the court of appeals shall be considered as having been filed in this Court, and briefs not yet filed in the court of appeals on the date of the order of transfer shall be filed directly in this Court within the time prescribed for filing briefs when no transfer is ordered.

norms.heading: Transfer on Order of Court of Appeals

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 83 — Transfers From Court of Appeals to this Court

norms.text:
A case disposed of by an opinion, memorandum decision, written order, or order of dismissal in the court of appeals may be transferred to this Court by order of a majority of the participating judges, regular and special, on their own motion or on application of a party. Transfer may be ordered because of the general interest or importance of a question involved in the case or for the purpose of reexamining existing law.
Application by a party for such transfer shall be filed within fifteen days of the date on which the opinion, memorandum decision, written order, or order of dismissal is filed unless for good cause shown the court of appeals extends the time for filing.

No response to an application for transfer shall be filed unless requested by the court, and an order for transfer shall not be granted in the absence of such a request.
Motions for reconsideration of the court's action in refusing an application for transfer shall not be accepted or filed.

norms.heading: Transfer by This Court After Opinion by Court of Appeals

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 83 — Transfers From Court of Appeals to this Court

norms.text:
Transfer by this Court is an extraordinary remedy that is not part of the standard review process for purposes of federal habeas corpus review.

A case may be transferred by order of this Court on application of a party for any of the reasons specified in Rule 83.02 or for the reason that the opinion filed is contrary to a previous decision of an appellate court of this state. A party does not need to file an application for transfer pursuant to Rule 83.02 prior to filing an application for transfer with this Court.
Application for such transfer shall be filed in this Court within the later of:

(1) 15 days of the date on which the court of appeals denied transfer or overruled any Rule 84.17 post-disposition motion; or

(2) 30 days of the date on which the court of appeals files its opinion, memorandum decision, written order, or order of dismissal.
Upon a showing of good cause, an application for transfer may be filed out of time, but no application for transfer shall be filed if the court of appeals has issued its mandate that is still in effect.

No response to an application for transfer shall be filed unless requested by the Court.

Motions for reconsideration of the Court's action in refusing an application for transfer or in overruling a motion to file an application for transfer out of time shall not be accepted or filed.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 527 classe les voies de recours françaises entre voies ordinaires (appel, opposition) et extraordinaires (tierce opposition, révision, cassation). Les textes du Missouri prévoient l’appel, la réouverture ou le réexamen du jugement, les motions post-décisionnelles et le transfert extraordinaire, mais pas cette classification complète ni tous ces recours.
correspondences.note_en: Article 527 classifies French remedies as ordinary (appeal, opposition) and extraordinary (third-party opposition, revision, cassation). The Missouri provisions separately provide for appeal, post-disposition review, relief from judgment, and extraordinary transfer, but do not establish the same complete classification or all of those remedies.

norms.heading: Application – Form – Contents

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 83 — Transfers From Court of Appeals to this Court

norms.text:
(a) The application for transfer mentioned in Rules 83.01, 83.02, and 83.04 may not exceed 12 pages.

(b) The applicant shall concisely set out on the first page of the application the questions of general interest and importance, the existing law that requires reexamination, and the opinions of the appellate courts of this state that are contrary to the opinion of the court of appeals sought to be reviewed. The application may allege more than one ground, concurrently or in the alternative.
(c) The applicant shall express the ground or grounds for transfer in the terms and circumstances of the case but without unnecessary detail. The matters shall be set out in short and concise terms that are not argumentative or repetitious. No other information shall appear on the page setting out the reasons for seeking transfer.

The failure to set out necessary matters with accuracy, brevity, and clearness shall be sufficient reason for denying the application.
(d) The remainder of the application shall contain a statement of the facts pertinent to the application and a discussion of the legal basis upon which the applicant seeks transfer.

(e) Exhibits consisting of written documents that are included in or attached to the application shall be counted as part of the application for purposes of the page limitation contained in Rule 83.05(a). No other exhibits shall be included in or attached to the application or shall otherwise be filed.
(f) The application for transfer filed in this Court shall be accompanied by a cover page substantially in conformity with Civil Procedure Form No. 15 and by the following:

(1) The opinion or order of disposition of the court of appeals;

(2) Any Rule 84.17 post-disposition motion and application for transfer filed in the court of appeals and a copy of any notice or order from the court of appeals overruling or denying the same;
(3) The docket fee in the amount specified by Rule 81.04; and

(4) Proof of notice to the clerk of the court of appeals.

(g) All parties shall be served pursuant to Rule 84.026 with a copy of any application for transfer on or before the date of filing.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article accorde un délai d’un mois pour présenter des observations après la transmission et impose, dans certains cas, la signature d’un avocat aux Conseils. Rule 84.05 prévoit des délais de dépôt de mémoires en appel, tandis que Rule 84.01 prévoit une exigence générale de signature, mais aucun ne reprend cette procédure ni ce délai.
correspondences.note_en: The article grants one month to submit observations after transmission and, in specified cases, requires signature by counsel admitted before the relevant courts. Rule 84.05 sets appellate brief deadlines and Rule 84.01 contains a general signature requirement, but neither reproduces this procedure or deadline.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 927 impose de nombreuses mentions et pièces à peine d’irrecevabilité, ainsi que la signature des avocats. Les règles du Missouri exigent notamment l’identification des appelants, du jugement et de la juridiction, ainsi que la signature des actes, mais ne reprennent pas l’ensemble des exigences françaises.
correspondences.note_en: Article 927 imposes extensive identifying information, attachments, appeal specifications, and attorney signatures on pain of inadmissibility. Missouri provisions require key notice-of-appeal information and signatures, but do not reproduce the full set of French requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet aux parties de se défendre elles-mêmes ou d’être assistées ou représentées, avec un pouvoir spécial pour le représentant non avocat. La Rule 84.01 reconnaît la signature par une partie non représentée, tandis que la Rule 88.09 encadre spécifiquement les parties sans avocat dans certaines affaires familiales.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows parties to appear on their own or to be assisted or represented, requiring a special authorization for a non-lawyer representative. Rule 84.01 recognizes filing by a self-represented party, while Rule 88.09 regulates self-represented parties specifically in certain domestic-relations proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1028 organise le dépôt devant le premier président d’une demande spéciale en faux et exige, lorsque le ministère est obligatoire, la signature d’un avocat aux Conseils. Les règles 84.025 et 84.01 prévoient respectivement le dépôt devant la juridiction d’appel et la signature des actes, sans instituer la demande en faux ni l’exigence d’un avocat spécialisé.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1028 governs filing a special forgery claim before the first president and requires, where representation is mandatory, signature by a specialized appellate lawyer. Rules 84.025 and 84.01 address appellate filing and signatures, but do not create a forgery proceeding or require specialized counsel.

correspondences.note_fr: Les observations des parties, lorsque la représentation est obligatoire, doivent être signées par un avocat aux Conseils. Les textes du Missouri imposent une signature ou attribution à un avocat de référence, mais ne prévoient pas la qualification spéciale d’avocat aux Conseils.
correspondences.note_en: Where representation is mandatory, party observations must be signed by an avocat aux Conseils. Missouri requires motions and pleadings to be signed or attributed to an attorney of record, but does not impose the French specialized-qualification requirement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose, à peine de nullité, l’identification des parties, de la décision attaquée et de la décision de la CEDH, ainsi que la constitution et la signature de l’avocat. Les textes du Missouri prévoient certains éléments des petitions ou notices et la signature, sans reprendre toutes ces exigences.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires, on pain of nullity, identification of the parties, challenged decision, and ECHR decision, plus counsel’s appearance and signature. Missouri provisions require some contents for petitions or notices and signatures, but not all of these particulars or the same sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: Le défendeur doit, sous peine d’irrecevabilité d’office, déposer dans les deux mois un mémoire en réponse signé par un avocat et le notifier à l’avocat du demandeur. Rule 84.05 prévoit le délai de dépôt du mémoire du défendeur, tandis que Rules 84.01 et 43.01 concernent respectivement la signature et la notification, avec des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The respondent must, on pain of dismissal or rejection ex officio, file within two months a response signed by counsel and serve it on claimant’s counsel. Rule 84.05 sets a respondent’s appellate-brief deadline, while Rules 84.01 and 43.01 address signatures and service under materially different conditions.

norms.heading: Docketing Cases

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 84 — Procedure in All Appellate Courts

norms.text:
After the notice of appeal has been filed, a docketing conference may be set by the court for the purpose of preparing a schedule for the filing of the record on appeal, including the transcript, and the briefs and considering the consolidation of related appeals. At a conference in a civil appeal the court may, inter alia, examine its jurisdiction and explore with the parties the possibility of settlement.
When the record on appeal is filed in the appellate court the case shall be docketed. Cases may be set for argument and submission in such order as the court deems advisable.

Appellate review of cases appealed under section 188.028.2(5), RSMo, shall be expedited.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article impose au greffe un répertoire général recensant les affaires et plusieurs éléments d'identification et de suivi. Les textes du Missouri prévoient le dépôt et le docketing des affaires ainsi qu'un docket sheet récapitulatif, mais sans registre général présentant exactement ces mentions.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the clerk to maintain a general register of cases and specified identifying and procedural information. Missouri provisions require filing and docketing, and an appellate docket sheet or case record, but do not establish a general register with the same contents.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 905 organise l’orientation d’une affaire devant la cour d’appel : fixation d’une audience à bref délai ou désignation d’un conseiller de la mise en état, avec information du greffe. La Rule 84.02 prévoit une conférence de mise au rôle et l’établissement d’un calendrier pour le dossier et les écritures, mais sans ces deux modalités ni l’invitation à une procédure participative.
correspondences.note_en: Article 905 governs appellate case orientation: expedited scheduling or designation of a case-management judge, with notice by the clerk. Rule 84.02 provides an appellate docketing conference and scheduling for the record and briefs, serving a comparable case-management function but not reproducing the French alternatives or participatory-procedure invitation.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 912 organise l’examen de l’affaire, le calendrier de mise en état, la clôture, les plaidoiries et la radiation en cas d’inaction. La Rule 84.02 permet une conférence de mise au rôle et l’établissement d’un calendrier d’appel; les Rules 84.05, 44.01 et 84.08 couvrent seulement certains délais, extensions et défauts.
correspondences.note_en: Article 912 organizes case review, a case-management schedule, closure, argument, and dismissal for procedural inactivity. Rule 84.02 permits a docketing conference and scheduling in an appeal, while Rules 84.05, 44.01, and 84.08 address only portions of the timing, extension, and default consequences.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 84.02 concerne la mise au rôle des appels et leur fixation pour argumentation, mais elle ne règle ni le délai nécessaire à la préparation de la défense, ni la réassignation, ni le jugement en l'absence de l'intimé.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 84.02 addresses appellate docketing and setting cases for argument, but it does not address preparation time, reassignment, or judgment when the respondent has not appeared.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 924 permet à l'intimé constitué de demander la fixation d'une audience dans les deux mois de l'appel. La Rule 84.02 prévoit une conférence de mise au rôle et la fixation de l'affaire pour argumentation, et RSMo 512.150 habilite les juridictions d'appel à fixer les délais et l'ordre des audiences, sans reprendre ce délai ni cette initiative de l'intimé.
correspondences.note_en: Article 924 allows an appearing respondent to request that a hearing be set within two months after the appeal. Rule 84.02 provides appellate docketing and setting for argument, and RSMo 512.150 authorizes rules on docketing and hearing dates, but neither adopts the same deadline or respondent-initiated mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le premier président fixe la date et l’heure d’appel de l’affaire, peut désigner la chambre de distribution et en avise les avocats constitués. La Rule 84.02 prévoit la mise au rôle et la fixation de l’affaire pour argumentation, tandis que le RSMo 512.150 habilite les cours à régler ces modalités, sans reprendre la désignation de chambre ni l’avis prévu.
correspondences.note_en: The first president sets the date and time for calling the case, may designate the assigned chamber, and notifies counsel. Rule 84.02 addresses docketing and setting appellate cases for argument, while RSMo 512.150 authorizes rules on those matters, but neither covers chamber designation and notice in the same terms.

correspondences.note_fr: Le magistrat homologue l’accord soumis par les parties. RSMo 517.111 prévoit l’entrée immédiate du jugement de consentement, mais non une procédure générale d’homologation; Rule 84.02 permet seulement d’explorer une transaction en appel.
correspondences.note_en: The assigned judge approves an agreement submitted by the parties. RSMo 517.111 provides for prompt entry of a consent judgment, but not general approval proceedings; Rule 84.02 merely permits settlement discussions in an appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1012 organise, devant la Cour de cassation, la désignation d’un rapporteur ainsi qu’une médiation ou une audience de règlement amiable, sous des conditions propres au pourvoi. La Rule 88.04 prévoit la médiation judiciaire et la Rule 84.02 permet d’explorer un règlement lors d’une conférence, mais dans des cadres et avec des effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1012 governs, before the French Court of Cassation, appointment of a reporting judge and mediation or an amicable-settlement hearing, subject to appeal-specific conditions. Rule 88.04 provides court-ordered mediation and Rule 84.02 permits settlement discussions at a docketing conference, but their settings and effects materially differ.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1037-1 organise la procédure devant la cour de renvoi après cassation : fixation accélérée, signification de la saisine, délais de conclusions, intervention et sanctions de caducité ou d’irrecevabilité. Les Rules 84.05, 84.026, 84.08 et 84.02 traitent respectivement des délais de mémoires, de la notification, du défaut de procédure et de la mise au rôle, mais sans régime spécifique de renvoi après cassation.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1037-1 governs proceedings on remand after cassation, including expedited scheduling, service of the remand filing, briefing deadlines, intervention, and sanctions for default. Rules 84.05, 84.026, 84.08, and 84.02 address briefing deadlines, service, procedural default, and docketing, but do not create a specific post-cassation remand procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que l’appel est formé en matière contentieuse et qu’il est instruit et jugé selon les règles de première instance. Les règles du Missouri régissent la formation de l’appel, la date à laquelle le jugement devient définitif et la mise au rôle, mais ne reprennent pas expressément l’application des règles de première instance.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that the appeal is taken as a contentious appeal and is processed and decided under the first-instance rules. Missouri rules govern commencing the appeal, finality of the judgment, and docketing, but do not expressly provide that first-instance rules govern the appellate proceedings.

norms.heading: Format of Documents

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 84 — Procedure in All Appellate Courts

norms.text:
(a) Briefs filed in the appellate courts shall conform to the requirements of Rule 84.06. Transcripts filed in the appellate courts shall conform to the requirements of Rule 81.12.

(b) Except as provided by local court rules, all other documents filed in the appellate courts shall conform to the following provisions:
(1) Documents shall be legible, formatted for pages of size 8 ½ x 11 inches, and have all pages, including the cover page, consecutively paginated using Arabic numerals at the bottom.
(2) Documents shall have a left, right, top, and bottom margin of not less than one inch and shall have line spacing not less than 1.5, except that the following may be single-spaced: the caption; headings; quotations more than two lines long; footnotes; certificate of service or other certificates required by Rule 84.06(c); and signature block. Page numbers may appear in the bottom margin, but no other text may appear in the margins.
(3) The font, including footnotes, shall not be smaller than 13 point, Times New Roman.

(c) The following documents shall be filed in text searchable PDF, except those filed by parties ineligible for electronic filing:

(1) Applications and Motions;

(2) Suggestions;

(3) Briefs;
(4) Petitions for a Writ; and

(5) Answers and Returns to a Writ.

norms.heading: Briefs – Contents

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 84 — Procedure in All Appellate Courts

norms.text:
(a) Contents. The brief for appellant shall contain:

(1) A detailed table of contents, with page references, and a table of cases (alphabetically arranged), statutes, and other authorities cited, with reference to the pages of the brief where they are cited;

(2) A concise statement of the grounds on which jurisdiction of the review court is invoked;
(3) A statement of facts;

(4) The points relied on;

(5) An argument, which shall substantially follow the order of the points relied on; and

(6) A short conclusion stating the precise relief sought.
(b) Jurisdictional Statement. Bare recitals that jurisdiction is invoked "on the ground that the case involves the validity of a statute" or similar statements or conclusions are insufficient as jurisdictional statements. The jurisdictional statement shall set forth sufficient factual data to demonstrate the applicability of the particular provision or provisions of article V, section 3, of the Constitution upon which jurisdiction is sought to be predicated.
For example: "The action is one involving the question of whether the respondent's machinery and equipment used in its operations in removing rock from the ground are exempt from the state sales tax law as being machinery and equipment falling within the exemption provided by section 144.030.3(4), RSMo, and hence involves the construction of a revenue law of this state."
(c) Statement of Facts. The statement of facts shall be a fair and concise statement of the facts relevant to the questions presented for determination without argument. All statement of facts shall have specific page references to the relevant portion of the record on appeal, i.e., legal file, transcript, or exhibits. If the citation is to the system-generated legal file, it shall include the system-generated appeal document number and page number (e.g., D6 p.
7). If the portion cited is contained in the appendix, a page reference to the appendix shall also be included (e.g., D6 p. 7; App 9).

(d) Points Relied On.

(1) Where the appellate court reviews the decision of a trial court, each point shall:

(A) Identify the trial court ruling or action that the appellant challenges;
(B) State concisely the legal reasons for the appellant's claim of reversible error; and

(C) Explain in summary fashion why, in the context of the case, those legal reasons support the claim of reversible error.

The point shall be in substantially the following form: "The trial court erred in [identify the challenged ruling or action], because [state the legal reasons for the claim of reversible error], in that [explain why the legal reasons, in the context of the case, support the claim of reversible error]."
(2) Where the appellate court reviews the decision of an administrative agency, rather than a trial court, each point shall:

(A) Identify the administrative ruling or action the appellant challenges;

(B) State concisely the legal reasons for the appellant's claim of reversible error; and

(C) Explain in summary fashion why, in the context of the case, those legal reasons support the claim of reversible error.
The point shall be in substantially the following form: "The [name of agency] erred in [identify the challenged ruling or action], because [state the legal reasons for the claim of reversible error, including the reference to the applicable statute authorizing review], in that [explain why, in the context of the case, the legal reasons support the claim of reversible error]."
(3) In an original writ proceeding, each point shall:

(A) State what relief the petitioner or relator seeks from the appellate court;

(B) Identify the action that the petitioner or relator challenges;

(C) State concisely the legal reasons for the challenge to respondent's action; and

(D) Explain in summary fashion why, in the context of the case, those legal reasons support the challenge.
For an action in prohibition, the point shall be in substantially the following form: "Relator is entitled to an order prohibiting Respondent from [describe challenged action], because [state the legal reasons for the challenge], in that [explain why, in the context of the case, the legal reasons support the challenge]." For other remedial writs, the introductory language should be altered appropriately.
(4) Abstract statements of law, standing alone, do not comply with this rule. Any reference to the record shall be limited to the ultimate facts necessary to inform the appellate court and the other parties of the issues. Detailed evidentiary facts shall not be included.

(5) Immediately following each "Point Relied On," the appellant, relator, or petitioner shall include a list of cases, not to exceed four, and the constitutional, statutory, and regulatory provisions or other authority upon which that party principally relies.
(6) If a party asserts error relating to damages, the party may assert its material effect on the judgment, including that the judgment is inadequate or excessive, in the same "Point Relied On."

(e) Argument. The argument shall substantially follow the order of "Points Relied On." The point relied on shall be restated at the beginning of the section of the argument discussing that point. The argument shall be limited to those errors included in the "Points Relied On."
For each claim of error, the argument shall also include a concise statement describing whether the error was preserved for appellate review; if so, how it was preserved; and the applicable standard of review.

If a point relates to the giving, refusal or modification of an instruction, such instruction shall be set forth in full in the argument portion of the brief.
Long quotations from cases and long lists of citations should not be included.

All factual assertions in the argument shall have specific page references to the relevant portion of the record on appeal, i.e., legal file, transcript, or exhibits. If the citation is to the system-generated legal file, it shall include the system-generated appeal document number and page number (e.g., D6 p. 7). If the portion cited is contained in the appendix, a page reference to the appendix shall also be included (e.g., D6 p. 7; App 9).
(f) Respondent's Brief. The respondent's brief shall include a detailed table of contents, a detailed table of authorities, and an argument in conformity with this Rule 84.04.

If the respondent is dissatisfied with the accuracy or completeness of the jurisdictional statement or statement of facts in the appellant's brief, the respondent's brief may include a jurisdictional statement or statement of facts.
The argument portion of the respondent's brief shall contain headings identifying the points relied on contained in the appellant's brief to which each such argument responds. The respondent's brief may also include additional arguments in support of the judgment that are not raised by the points relied on in the appellant's brief.

(g) Reply Briefs. The appellant may file a reply brief but shall not reargue points covered in the appellant's initial brief.
(h) Appendix. A party’s brief shall be accompanied by a separate appendix containing the following materials, unless the material has been included in a previously filed appendix:

(1) The judgment, order, or decision in question, including the relevant findings of fact and conclusions of law filed in a judge-tried case or by an administrative agency;
(2) The complete text of all statutes, ordinances, rules of court, or agency rules claimed to be controlling as to a point on appeal; and

(3) The complete text of any instruction to which a point relied on relates.

An appendix also may set forth matters pertinent to the issues discussed in the brief such as copies of exhibits, excerpts from the written record, and copies of new cases or other pertinent authorities.
The appendix shall have a separate table of contents.

The pages in the appendix shall be numbered consecutively beginning with page A1. The inclusion of any matter in an appendix does not satisfy any requirement to set out such mater in a particular section of the brief.

An appendix to a brief on appeal, regardless of the number of pages it contains, shall be filed as a separate document.
(i) Cross Appeals. If a cross appeal is filed, the plaintiff in the court below shall be deemed the appellant for purposes of this Rule 84.04, unless the parties otherwise agree or the court otherwise orders. The appellant's initial brief shall be filed as otherwise provided in this Rule 84.04 and Rule 84.05.
The respondent's initial brief shall contain the issues and argument involved in the respondent's appeal and the response to the brief of the appellant. The appellant may file a second brief in response to the respondent's brief setting forth respondent's appeal and in reply to the respondent's brief opposing appellant's appeal. The respondent may file a reply brief in reply to appellant's response to the issues presented by respondent's appeal. The briefs otherwise shall comply with Rule 84.06. No further briefs shall be filed without leave of the court.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 85 exige que la déclaration identifie l’appel comme portant sur la compétence et soit motivée, puis prévoit une instruction selon une procédure accélérée ou spéciale. Les règles 81.04 et 512.070 imposent seulement l’identification de la décision, des parties et de la juridiction; la règle 84.04 exige ultérieurement des points d’appel motivés dans le mémoire.
correspondences.note_en: Article 85 requires the notice to identify the appeal as a jurisdiction appeal and to state its grounds, followed by expedited or special treatment. Rules 81.04 and 512.070 require basic identification only; Rule 84.04 later requires articulated grounds of error in the appellate brief.

correspondences.note_fr: La dévolution est limitée aux chefs du dispositif critiqués et à ceux qui en dépendent, sauf appel-annulation. Le Missouri exige que l'avis désigne le jugement attaqué et que les points d'appel identifient les erreurs, mais les textes fournis ne prévoient pas expressément la règle française des chefs dépendants ni la dévolution intégrale en cas d'annulation.
correspondences.note_en: Appellate jurisdiction is limited to expressly challenged dispositions and dependent dispositions, except when annulment is sought. Missouri requires designation of the judgment and specification of appellate errors, but the supplied provisions do not expressly provide the French dependent-issues rule or automatic total devolution upon annulment.

correspondences.note_fr: Le conseiller peut imposer la mise en conformité des conclusions, demander des explications et assurer la communication, l’obtention et la production des pièces. Les Rules 84.04, 81.12 et 81.16 réglementent respectivement le contenu des mémoires d’appel, le dossier d’appel et le dépôt des pièces, mais ne confèrent pas exactement les mêmes pouvoirs au juge chargé de la mise en état.
correspondences.note_en: The French rule empowers the case-management judge to enforce brief compliance, request explanations, and control the communication, obtaining, and production of evidence. Rules 84.04, 81.12, and 81.16 address appellate briefs, the appellate record, and exhibits, but do not grant the same comprehensive case-management powers.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article définit les conclusions d’appel recevables par leur dépôt au greffe, leur notification dans les délais et leur fonction de détermination de l’objet du litige. Les Rules 84.04 et 84.05 encadrent le contenu et les délais des mémoires, tandis que les Rules 43.01 et 43.02 régissent leur notification et leur dépôt.
correspondences.note_en: The article defines appellate submissions by their filing with the clerk, timely service, and role in determining the dispute. Rules 84.04 and 84.05 regulate brief contents and deadlines, while Rules 43.01 and 43.02 govern service and filing.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe les chefs critiqués par les premières conclusions et impose la présentation initiale de l’ensemble des prétentions au fond, sous réserve de certaines réponses ou demandes nouvelles. La Rule 84.04 structure les points et le relief demandé, tandis que les Rules 84.13 et le RSMo 512.160 limitent l’examen aux erreurs présentées et préservées.
correspondences.note_en: The article fixes the challenged judgment provisions through the first submissions and generally requires all merits claims to be presented initially, subject to specified later claims. Rule 84.04 structures appellate issues and relief, while Rule 84.13 and RSMo 512.160 limit review to properly presented and preserved matters.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une structure et un contenu détaillés aux conclusions d’appel, limite l’examen aux prétentions et moyens exposés, et prévoit la concentration dans les dernières conclusions. La Rule 84.04 règle également le contenu structuré des briefs et des points invoqués, tandis que la Rule 84.13 écarte les erreurs non ou mal soulevées, mais l’ensemble n’est pas identique.
correspondences.note_en: The article imposes detailed structure and content requirements for appellate submissions, limits review to the claims and arguments presented, and requires concentration in the latest submissions. Rule 84.04 likewise governs structured appellate briefs and points relied on, while Rule 84.13 excludes unbriefed or improperly briefed errors, but the coverage is not identical.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 978 impose le dépôt et la notification du mémoire dans un délai déterminé, ainsi qu’une présentation structurée et précise des moyens, sous sanctions. La Rule 84.04 encadre le contenu des briefs et des points invoqués ; les Rules 84.05, 84.026 et 84.08 prévoient respectivement les délais, le service et les conséquences des défauts.
correspondences.note_en: Article 978 requires timely filing and service of a structured memorandum, with precise grounds and sanctions for defects. Rule 84.04 governs brief contents and points relied on; Rules 84.05, 84.026, and 84.08 address deadlines, service, and consequences of default.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 989 impose, en l’absence de moyens dans la déclaration de pourvoi, un mémoire exposant ces moyens dans les trois mois, sous peine de déchéance. La Rule 84.04 exige la présentation des points d’appel, la Rule 84.05 fixe les délais de mémoires et la Rule 84.08 prévoit une sanction de rejet, mais selon un régime différent.
correspondences.note_en: Article 989 requires a memorandum stating the grounds when the appeal declaration lacks them, within three months and subject to forfeiture. Rule 84.04 requires appellate points, Rule 84.05 sets brief deadlines, and Rule 84.08 provides dismissal for procedural default, but the Missouri framework differs materially.

correspondences.note_fr: À défaut d'énoncé des moyens dans la déclaration, le demandeur doit déposer dans le mois un mémoire les exposant, sous peine d'irrecevabilité d'office. La Rule 84.04 exige que le mémoire d'appel expose les points invoqués et l'argumentation, mais les textes fournis ne permettent pas d'attribuer à cette règle un délai d'un mois ni une irrecevabilité d'office.
correspondences.note_en: If the appeal declaration lacks even a summary of the grounds, the appellant must file within one month a memorandum stating them, subject to dismissal for inadmissibility. Rule 84.04 requires appellate briefs to state the points relied on and argument, but the supplied text does not impose the one-month deadline or automatic inadmissibility.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au pourvoi incident la forme d’un mémoire, des indications déterminées, des délais de dépôt et de notification, ainsi qu’un mémoire en réponse. Les Rules 84.05 et 84.04 concernent les délais et le contenu des briefs, tandis que les Rules 43.01 et 43.02 régissent leur signification et leur dépôt, sans mécanisme identique de pourvoi incident.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires an incidental appeal to take the form of a memorandum, with specified contents, filing and service deadlines, and a response memorandum. Rules 84.05 and 84.04 address brief deadlines and contents, while Rules 43.01 and 43.02 govern service and filing, but none creates the same incidental-appeal mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au demandeur un mémoire motivé dans un délai de deux mois, sa notification aux autres parties et une sanction de déchéance. Les Rules 84.04 et 84.05 encadrent le contenu et les délais des mémoires d’appel, tandis que la Rule 84.08 prévoit une radiation en cas de défaut, mais dans un régime différent.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a reasoned memorandum within two months, service on the other parties, and forfeiture for noncompliance. Rules 84.04 and 84.05 regulate appellate brief contents and deadlines, while Rule 84.08 addresses dismissal for procedural default, under a different regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exige que l’appelant précise lorsqu’il limite son appel à un chef de décision. Les règles du Missouri exigent l’identification de la décision attaquée et, dans les écritures ou un état convenu, la formulation des points invoqués, sans reprendre exactement cette obligation de préciser les chefs limités.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires an appellant to specify when the appeal is limited to a particular ruling. Missouri provisions require identification of the judgment or order and formulation of the points relied on, but do not impose the same express requirement to identify limited grounds of appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article soumet l’appel et le recours en annulation aux règles de la procédure contentieuse d’appel. Les règles du Missouri régissent également la formation de l’appel, le dossier et les mémoires, mais ne prévoient pas dans les textes fournis un régime spécifique applicable aux recours contre les sentences arbitrales.
correspondences.note_en: The article subjects the appeal and annulment action to ordinary contentious appellate procedure. The Missouri provisions likewise govern commencement of an appeal, the appellate record, and briefs, but the supplied texts contain no special procedure for review of arbitral awards.

norms.heading: Briefs – When and By Whom Filed

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 84 — Procedure in All Appellate Courts

norms.text:
(a) Time of Filing. Within 60 days after the date on which the record on appeal is filed with the clerk of the appellate court, the appellant shall file the appellant's brief. Within 30 days after the filing of appellant's brief, respondent shall file respondent's brief. Within 15 days after the filing of respondent's brief, the appellant may file a reply brief. The appellate court may, by order in specific cases, either shorten or lengthen the periods prescribed above for filing briefs.
(b) Time of Filing in Cross Appeals. Within 60 days after the date on which the record on appeal is filed with the clerk of the appellate court, the appellant shall file appellant's brief. Within 30 days after the filing of the appellant's brief, respondent/cross-appellant shall file respondent/cross-appellant's brief. Within 30 days after the filing of respondent/cross-appellant's brief, appellant may file appellant's brief in response to the cross appeal and in reply to the respondent's brief. Within 15 days thereafter, the cross-appellant may file cross-appellant's reply brief.
The appellate court may, by order in specific cases, either shorten or lengthen the time prescribed above for filing briefs.
(c) Where Trial Court Fails to Specify Grounds for the Granting of a New Trial. When a trial court grants a new trial without specifying of record the ground or grounds on which the new trial is granted, the presumption shall be that the trial court erroneously granted the motion for new trial and the burden of supporting such action is placed on the respondent.
In such event, if the appellant files a statement requesting that respondent prepare the original brief on or before the time when the record on appeal is filed, the respondent shall file the original brief and reply brief, if any, within the time otherwise required for the appellant to file briefs. The appellant shall file the answer brief in the time otherwise required for the respondent to file the respondent's brief.
(d) Where New Trial Is Granted by Trial Court Without Specifying Discretionary Grounds. If the trial court grants a new trial without specifying discretionary grounds, it shall never be presumed that the new trial was granted on any discretionary grounds.
(e) Where Circuit Court Reverses a Decision of An Administrative Agency. If the circuit court reverses a decision of an administrative agency and the appellate court reviews the decision of the agency rather than of the circuit court, a party aggrieved by the circuit court decision shall file a notice of appeal and the record on appeal and shall file with the record on appeal a notice designating the party that is aggrieved by the agency decision. The party aggrieved by the agency decision shall file the appellant's brief and reply brief, if any, within the time otherwise required for the appellant to file briefs.
If a party who is aggrieved by an agency decision fails to file the first brief, that party shall be given notice of dismissal as required in Rule 84.08.

(f) Briefs and Suggestions of Amicus Curiae in This Court.
(1) Suggestions may be filed in this Court by amicus curiae in support of or in opposition to the granting of applications for transfer. Such suggestions are not favored. The suggestions shall only be filed with the consent of all parties or upon order of this Court. The suggestions shall not exceed five pages and shall be filed only if submitted a reasonable time prior to consideration by this Court of the application. Consideration of the application by this Court shall not be delayed pending receipt of the suggestions.
(2) A brief may be filed by amicus curiae in cases before this Court on the merits. The brief shall only be filed with the consent of all parties or upon order of this Court. The brief shall only be filed if presented for filing within the time allowed for the filing of the brief of the party supported.
(3) If consent to the filing of suggestions or a brief by amicus curiae is refused by a party to the case, a motion for leave to file may be filed with this Court. The motion for leave to file shall identify the parties refusing consent, concisely state the nature of the applicant's interest, and set forth facts or questions of law that have not been, or reasons for believing that they will not be, presented adequately by the parties, and their relevancy to the disposition of the case.
The motion shall not exceed five pages. The brief shall be conditionally filed with the motion for leave. A party may file an objection to the filing of a brief of an amicus curiae concisely stating the reasons for withholding consent.

(4) Consent to the filing of suggestions or a brief of an amicus curiae need not be had when the suggestions or brief are presented by the attorney general or by a state entity authorized by law to appear on its own behalf.
(5) All suggestions and briefs filed by amicus curiae shall conform with Rule 84.03 and Rule 84.06, respectively.
